Trend or Sideways? — ER vs ADX vs Choppiness vs MA Slope vs Bollinger Width

On this page

  1. 1. What each tool actually measures
  2. 2. Test A — can any of them predict the next 10 days?
  3. 3. Test B — do they help a trend-follower?
  4. 4. Which one is better for what
  5. 5. Settings and reading tips
  6. 6. One-line summary

Five common ways to tell whether a market is trending or going sideways: what each one measures, what it is good for, and what my own test on 185 Nifty 200 stocks (daily, 2014–Oct 2026, ~484k stock-days) showed. Education, not investment advice. KAMA and the Efficiency Ratio in detail: kama_kaufman_adaptive_moving_average.md.

1. What each tool actually measures

ToolFormula ideaMeasuresGives direction?Speed
Efficiency Ratio (ER, 10)net move ÷ total pathhow straight price movednofast (raw, no smoothing)
ADX (14)smoothed |+DI − −DI| ÷ (+DI + −DI)how one-sided the bars are (higher highs vs lower lows)no (+DI vs −DI does)slow (double-smoothed, ~2×14 bars of lag)
Choppiness Index (14)log(Σ true range ÷ 14-bar high–low range)how much of the bars' movement was wasted inside the rangenomedium
MA slope (50-SMA, 10-bar change ÷ ATR)how fast the average is rising/fallingthe direction and pace of the trendyesslow (MA lag)
Bollinger Band width (20, 2)4 × std dev ÷ 20-SMAvolatility, not trendnomedium

Overlap (rank correlation between the tools, my data):

  • ER and Choppiness overlap a lot (−0.55): two versions of "net move vs total movement". You don't need both.
  • Choppiness and BB width −0.59; ADX and BB width +0.44: big trends usually come with big ranges.
  • MA slope has almost no correlation with any of the others (≤ 0.17). It is the only one that tells you which way.

2. Test A — can any of them predict the next 10 days?

Rank correlation between today's value and the next 10 days' trendiness (ER), volatility change, and size of the move:

Tool→ next-10-day ER (trendiness)→ volatility expansion→ next |move| ÷ ATR
ER−0.02+0.05+0.01
ADX−0.03−0.05−0.03
Choppiness+0.02+0.08+0.01
MA slope−0.02+0.00+0.00
BB width (percentile)−0.04−0.23−0.07
  • None of them predicts whether the next 10 days will trend or chop. Trending stocks and sideways stocks are followed by trendiness of about 0.28–0.31 either way.
  • Only Bollinger width predicts something: volatility. After a squeeze (width in the bottom 20% of the last year), the next 10 days' volatility was 10% higher than the last 20 days' (ratio 1.10). After very wide bands it was 18% lower (0.82). Volatility goes back toward normal. The squeeze tells you "a bigger move is likely". It does not tell you which way.

3. Test B — do they help a trend-follower?

Bet in the direction of the 50-day SMA slope, then measure the average 20-day return in that direction. Compare each tool's "trending" and "sideways" readings. Gross returns, before charges.

State todayShare of daysAvg 20-day return in trend directionHit rate
All days (no filter)100%+0.25%50.6%
Choppiness < 3812%+0.66%52.3%
ADX > 2543%+0.46%51.4%
|MA slope| > 1 ATR25%+0.46%51.5%
ER > 0.523%+0.43%51.1%
BB squeeze (bottom 20%)22%+0.29%51.0%
ER < 0.235%+0.22%50.8%
ADX < 2036%+0.15%50.5%
Choppiness > 6210%+0.14%50.4%
|MA slope| < 0.25 ATR22%+0.03%50.0%
  • Every "trending" filter roughly doubles the trend-follower's edge, and every "sideways" reading roughly kills it. So yes, they separate good conditions for trend-following from bad ones.
  • The hit rate hardly moves (50% → 51–52%). The gain comes from bigger winning moves, not more frequent wins.
  • Choppiness < 38 was strongest but is rare (12% of days). ADX > 25 and MA slope were almost as good and cover 25–43% of days.
  • ADX rising vs falling made no difference (+0.47% vs +0.43%), despite the popular rule "only trade when ADX is rising".
  • The edge is small. +0.5% per 20 days gross is about the size of a delivery round trip's charges plus slippage (~0.3–0.4%), so a filter on its own is not a tradable strategy. It only improves a signal that already has an edge.

But look at it year by year (avg 20-day return in trend direction, %):

YearNo filter|slope| > 1ADX > 25ER > 0.5
2018−0.70−1.14−1.46−0.57
2022−0.17−0.93−0.22+0.13
2023+1.49+2.53+2.66+2.09
2024+1.31+2.15+1.73+1.35
2026−0.48−1.53−1.15−0.44

The filters mostly amplify the year: in trend-friendly years (2021, 2023–24) they make it better, and in choppy, reversing years (2018, 2026) they make it worse (ER > 0.5 was the exception in 2022). "Trending right now" is not "will keep trending". This is the same lesson as Test A, seen through returns.

4. Which one is better for what

You want to…UseWhy
Know which way to tradeMA slope (or price vs 200-DMA)The only one with direction. My best filter so far is Nifty above its 200-DMA (+0.26 Sharpe in ../backtests/backtest_results_summary.md)
Turn a trend system on or offADX > 25 (simple, common) or Choppiness < 38 (stricter, rarer)Both separated good and bad trend-following days best in Test B. Don't bother with "ADX rising"
Avoid trading in chopChoppiness > 62 or |MA slope| < 0.25 ATRTrend-following made ~0% in these states
Make an indicator adapt its own speedER (inside KAMA)Fast, no smoothing lag, a clean 0–1 scale. Built to be plugged into a formula
Expect a big move / size positions / optionsBB width (squeeze)The only tool that predicted anything: volatility expands after a squeeze, shrinks after wide bands. No direction
Mean-reversion (range) tradingADX < 20 + Choppiness > 62Shows the market is going nowhere now, but test Test A again: chop doesn't reliably continue either

Practical combo: direction from MA slope / 200-DMA, permission from ADX or Choppiness, size from ATR or BB width. ER and Choppiness are nearly the same, so pick one of them.

5. Settings and reading tips

  • ADX: 14 is standard. Under 20 is no trend; over 25 is a trend; over 40 is a strong trend that may be stretched. It is slow: by the time ADX crosses 25 the trend is usually weeks old. +DI above −DI means uptrend.
  • Choppiness: 14 bars. The 38.2 / 61.8 lines are Fibonacci levels, but they are just thresholds. 100 = pure chop, 0 = straight line.
  • ER: 10 bars. Thresholds depend on the window length (Nifty median 0.31 at n = 10, 0.13 at n = 60), so use percentiles.
  • MA slope: divide by ATR so the number means the same on a ₹100 stock and a ₹10,000 stock.
  • BB width: compare with its own last year (percentile), never as a raw number across stocks.
  • Timeframe: on 15-min or 1-hour bars, all of these flip between "trend" and "chop" many times a day. Use daily or weekly.

6. One-line summary

MA slope tells you which way; ADX or Choppiness tell you whether trend-following is worth it right now; ER drives adaptive indicators like KAMA; BB width predicts volatility, not direction. None of them predicts whether the next period will trend.
